traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements for story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md are implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality: The plugin is implemented in TypeScript (src/index.ts) with a standard ESLint plugin shape (default export with rules/configs, plus named exports). Tests in tests/plugin-setup.test.ts and tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts confirm that rules and configs are exported correctly and that the rules registry contains the expected rule names. - Quality Standards: The plugin follows ESLint plugin conventions: namespaced rule keys, default export plugin object, documented configs.recommended/strict, and a dynamic rule loader that supports CJS/ESM. The code is typed, structured, and tested according to typical ESLint plugin best practices. - Integration with ESLint v9 flat config: eslint.config.js is a proper flat config that loads the plugin from src/lib, attaches it under the traceability namespace, and configures rules for JS/TS and tests. Integration tests in tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts and dogfooding-validation.test.ts spawn ESLint v9 with this config and assert correct behavior (rules triggered, non-zero exit codes), demonstrating working integration. - User Experience: README.md and the user-docs/ directory provide clear installation instructions, flat-config examples, quick start, and validation steps. These cover both basic plugin setup and realistic configuration patterns, satisfying the setup and UX expectations of the story. - Error Handling: The dynamic rule loader in src/index.ts wraps each rule require in try/catch, logs a descriptive error, and installs a placeholder rule that reports a clear diagnostic when executed. tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts and tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts validate this behavior end-to-end; all such tests passed in the Jest run. - Documentation: Root README plus dedicated user docs (eslint-9-setup-guide, API reference, examples, migration guide) document plugin structure, installation, configuration, and development/testing setup. This satisfies the story’s documentation acceptance criterion and definition of done around documentation and testability.
Given the passing, story-referenced tests and the concrete implementation and documentation evidence, this story is fully implemented.
